1	// The request implementer (tasks-dispatch DESIGN §16) — the engine's one built-in
2	// task, and the only one that may read an item's `Model`.
3	//
4	// A person marks an ordinary issue `task:origin:ad-hoc`; the scheduler run adopts
5	// it by writing the machine block onto that issue and applying the first status —
6	// the issue IS the item (§16.1); this task's precondition decides, at pickup,
7	// whether the run happens; the session implements the issue and leaves a pull
8	// request. There is no code-work phase at all: the authorization a worker would
9	// have performed is the precondition's, and the item's `Request:` field — which
10	// names the item's own issue — is the whole payload.
11	
12	// Push permission, as the permission API answers it. `triage` and `read` are
13	// deliberately not here: the ask was push access, and a read-only collaborator
14	// rides every webhook payload as `COLLABORATOR` (F30).
15	export const PUSH_PERMISSIONS = ['admin', 'maintain', 'write'];
16	
17	// Who, if anyone, with push access asked for this. Pure over the `request` signal's
18	// read, so the judgment is testable without GitHub and the reads stay where every
19	// other read is.
20	export function eligibility(req) {
21	  if (PUSH_PERMISSIONS.includes(req.authorPermission)) {
22	    return { ok: true, why: `opened by @${req.author}, who has push access` };
23	  }
24	  const blessed = (req.approvals ?? []).find((a) => PUSH_PERMISSIONS.includes(a.permission));
25	  if (blessed) return { ok: true, why: `approved by @${blessed.login} with \`/claude go\`` };
26	  return { ok: false, why: 'neither opened nor approved with `/claude go` by anyone with push access on this repository' };
27	}
28	
29	export default {
30	  // The literal, not the constant beside it in `built-in-tasks.mjs`: the
31	  // declaration-shape check reads this file statically and cannot resolve an
32	  // import. The two are pinned to each other in request-mode.test.mjs.
33	  id: 'implement-request',
34	  // MANUAL: the scheduler run never puts this on a calendar. An item exists only because an
35	  // issue was marked, which is what makes a request a first-class origin of work
36	  // rather than a schedule nobody asked for.
37	  frequency: 'manual',
38	  // The read the precondition judges on. It is collected for THIS item — the issue
39	  // its `Request:` field names — which is why the precondition takes the item.
40	  precondition_signals: ['request'],
41	  // The default when the asker named no family; the item's `Model:` overrides it,
42	  // and only because this task declares the field below.
43	  agent_model: 'opus',
44	  model_from_request: true,
45	  // The ceiling the executor enforces in code. The task's own policy is the full
46	  // `anything` because the REAL decider is per-request: the asker's `Automerge:`
47	  // becomes the item's `Merge:` field (§16.11), a policy expression the worker
48	  // hands to the policy engine, and the task ceiling must not sit below whatever
49	  // an asker may legitimately authorize. A ceiling is a maximum, not an
50	  // instruction: with no such field the worker opens a pull request and parks at
51	  // the approval lane exactly as every request did before, and with one it still
52	  // parks whenever the policy engine says the diff is not covered.
53	  expected_outcome: 'pr',
54	  automerge: 'anything',
55	  agent_instructions: 'task.md',
56	  agent_execution_timeout: 4 * 3600,
57	  // A run that died mid-flight leaves a branch, a PR, or neither, and only a person
58	  // can say whether the half-done work stands — so nothing re-queues it mechanically.
59	  on_interrupt: 'needs-human',
60	
61	  // THE SECURITY CHECK, and it happens where every verdict happens: once, at pickup,
62	  // on the executor (§6.4). Three refusals, each a plain no-go that converges the
63	  // item to the rejected terminal — a refusal is nobody's inbox, and an ad-hoc item
64	  // has no anchor to roll to. On a marked issue that terminal stands on the OPEN
65	  // issue: the run's verdict is not the issue's validity (§16.5).
66	  //
67	  // A READ FAILURE IS NOT A VERDICT (F27). The decline's write-back cannot reach an
68	  // issue it cannot read, so declining on a rate limit or a 500 would strand
69	  // `claude-queued` on the issue forever over nothing — the request silently eaten.
70	  // Only a definitive `gone` declines; anything else FAILS the run, which parks the
71	  // item open in the failure lane where the ordinary re-queue lever retries it.
72	  precondition(signals, config, item) {
73	    const req = signals.request;
74	    if (!req) {
75	      return { error: `this item names no readable request (its \`Request:\` field is ${item?.request ? `#${item.request}` : 'missing'})` };
76	    }
77	    if (req.unreadable) return { error: `issue #${req.number} could not be read: ${req.error} — refusing to guess` };
78	    if (req.gone) return { run: false, reason: `issue #${req.number} does not exist` };
79	    if (req.state !== 'open') return { run: false, reason: `issue #${req.number} was closed before this ran` };
80	    if (!req.queued) {
81	      return { run: false, reason: `issue #${req.number} no longer carries the mark — the request was withdrawn` };
82	    }
83	    const verdict = eligibility(req);
84	    return verdict.ok
85	      // No `context`: adoption already bound this item to its issue, and a second
86	      // line saying the same thing renders as two near-identical bullets in the one
87	      // section the session is told to read as its scope (seen on the first live
88	      // request, #1074/#1075).
89	      ? { run: true, reason: `#${req.number}: ${verdict.why}` }
90	      : { run: false, reason: `#${req.number}: ${verdict.why}` };
91	  },
92	};

27	// `task:` namespace. These are the spellings a reader compares against: decode

29	// version answers the same question the same way.
30	export const STATUS_PREFIX = 'task:status:';
31	export const PARK_PREFIX = `${STATUS_PREFIX}needs-human-`;
32	
33	export const STATUS_BLOCKED = `${STATUS_PREFIX}blocked`;
34	export const STATUS_READY = `${STATUS_PREFIX}waiting-for-executor`;

46	// swap's leavings, which the janitor repairs (DESIGN §6.2, §11).
47	export const LIVE_STATUSES = Object.freeze([
48	  STATUS_BLOCKED, STATUS_READY, STATUS_RUNNING_EXECUTOR, STATUS_RUNNING_AGENT,
49	]);

53	export const PARK_KINDS = Object.freeze(['failure', 'action', 'decision', 'approval']);
54	export const PARK_STATUSES = Object.freeze(PARK_KINDS.map((k) => `${PARK_PREFIX}${k}`));
55	export const STATUS_LABELS = Object.freeze([

59	// THE ORIGIN (DESIGN §3, decision §15.29) — who asked for this item, worn for the
60	// item's whole life beside whatever status it holds. Read here; the writers arrive

62	export const ORIGIN_PREFIX = 'task:origin:';
63	export const ORIGIN_PLANNED = `${ORIGIN_PREFIX}planned`;
64	export const ORIGIN_AD_HOC = `${ORIGIN_PREFIX}ad-hoc`;

66	export const ORIGIN_LABELS = Object.freeze([ORIGIN_PLANNED, ORIGIN_AD_HOC, ORIGIN_GITHUB]);

68	// --- the write spellings ------------------------------------------------------
69	// What this engine APPLIES — the canonical vocabulary above, since the write-side
70	// flip (#1119). The names survive the flip because fielded pack versions import

152	// WHICH PARKS HOLD THE TASK'S LANE. A task's open STANDING item is the occurrence
153	// itself, so while one exists the generator files no further occurrence
154	// (`planSchedulerRun` job 1) — which for a park means the task stops being scheduled at
155	// all until a human clears it. That is right for a `failure`: filing a queue of
156	// items that will break the same way helps nobody, and the silence is the signal.
157	// It is wrong for the other three, which are a person's inbox, not a fault in the

167	// --- the decode (DESIGN §4, "legacy spellings — written never, read forever") --
168	// Labels are STORED DATA: open items filed by a fielded engine wear its spellings,
169	// closed items keep theirs forever, and members converge on their own schedules. So
170	// every reader here goes through one pass that maps every spelling ever written
171	// straight to today's — never through a literal comparison against one of them.
172	const LEGACY_STATUS = new Map([
173	  [LEGACY_BLOCKED, STATUS_BLOCKED],
174	  [LEGACY_READY, STATUS_READY],
175	  [LEGACY_EXECUTING, STATUS_RUNNING_EXECUTOR],
176	  [LEGACY_AGENT, STATUS_RUNNING_AGENT],
177	  [LEGACY_TASK_DONE, STATUS_DONE], [OUTCOME_DONE, STATUS_DONE],
178	  [LEGACY_TASK_OBSOLETE, STATUS_REJECTED], [OUTCOME_OBSOLETE, STATUS_REJECTED],
179	]);

181	const LEGACY_PARK_RE = /^task:needs-human-(.+)$/;
182	
183	// The park an issue's labels name, canonical, or null. Both shapes decode here:
184	// today's single `task:status:needs-human-<kind>` and the legacy pair
185	// (`needs-human` plus a sub-label). A kind nobody here knows — a bare legacy park,
186	// or a word a newer engine invented — reads as `failure`, the conservative lane.
187	function parkOf(names) {
188	  const kinds = [
189	    ...names.filter((n) => n.startsWith(PARK_PREFIX)).map((n) => n.slice(PARK_PREFIX.length)),
190	    ...names.map((n) => LEGACY_PARK_RE.exec(n)?.[1]).filter(Boolean),
191	  ];
192	  if (!kinds.length && !names.includes(NEEDS_HUMAN)) return null;
193	  return `${PARK_PREFIX}${PARK_KINDS.find((k) => kinds.includes(k)) ?? 'failure'}`;
194	}

196	// Every distinct status an issue's labels decode to. One entry per status, so an
197	// item mid-flip — wearing a legacy spelling beside its canonical one — reads as the
198	// ONE status it is, and only genuinely conflicting labels read as more than one
199	// (the dashboard's `torn`).
200	export function statusesOn(issue) {
201	  const names = labelNames(issue);
202	  const out = new Set();
203	  const park = parkOf(names);
204	  if (park) out.add(park);
205	  for (const n of names) {
206	    if (STATUS_LABELS.includes(n) && !n.startsWith(PARK_PREFIX)) out.add(n);
207	    else if (LEGACY_STATUS.has(n)) out.add(LEGACY_STATUS.get(n));
208	  }
209	  return [...out];
210	}

215	export function statusOf(issue) {
216	  const worn = statusesOn(issue);
217	  return worn.find((s) => s.startsWith(PARK_PREFIX))
218	    ?? STATUS_LABELS.find((s) => worn.includes(s))
219	    ?? null;
220	}

262	// The one outcome an issue's labels carry, as the canonical word ('done',
263	// 'delivered', 'obsolete') or null. Everything that tallies or renders outcomes
264	// decodes through here, so a spelling change is one map entry and not a sweep.

269	  const worn = statusesOn(issue);

341	// GitHub hands labels back as objects on the issues API and as bare strings in
342	// some fixtures; accept either.

348	// Title. The optional qualifier exists ONLY for deliberately concurrent items —
349	// a fan-out naming its target — and it is part of the identity the same-title
350	// mutex reads (DESIGN §6.1). Nothing ever encodes a date here: that was the slot
351	// grammar, and the issue number is the identity (DESIGN §5).
352	export const workItemTitle = ({ pack, task, qualifier = null }) =>
353	  `${WORK_PREFIX} ${pack}/${task}${qualifier ? ` ${qualifier}` : ''}`;
354	
355	// pack and task ids are single path segments; the qualifier is whatever follows.
356	const TITLE_RE = /^\[claudinite-work\]\s+([^/\s]+)\/([^/\s]+)(?:\s+(\S.*))?$/;

358	// The pack half is canonicalized on the way out. A work item's title is STORED
359	// DATA — it sits on an open GitHub issue that outlives any one converge — so items
360	// filed before a pack was renamed still carry the old spelling. Read literally, the
361	// scheduler run would not recognise its own live item, would file a second one beside it, and
362	// would leave the first orphaned in the queue with nothing ever draining it.
363	export function parseWorkItemTitle(title) {
364	  const m = TITLE_RE.exec(String(title ?? '').trim());
365	  return m ? { pack: canonicalPackId(m[1]), task: m[2], qualifier: m[3]?.trim() || null } : null;
366	}

370	// The `<pack>/<task>` id a WORKER PATH names — the identity half a marked issue's
371	// title cannot carry (DESIGN §16.1), read off the path its machine block names. Two
372	// shapes, because tasks have two homes: the `tasks/` slot a declared pack contributes,
373	// and the queue's own built-in root. The `.claudinite/shared/` prefix is optional in
374	// both — a member's mount is there and the canon runs its own tree.
375	//
376	// THE BUILT-IN ROOT HAS TWO SPELLINGS, and both are permanent. The surface moved from
377	// `engine/scheduler/` to the tasks pack (#1317), so a live item minted before the move
378	// still names the engine path while every new one names the pack path; the wire id
379	// either produces is unchanged, which is what the move promised. Stored data is
380	// renamed on the DECODE side or it stops decoding, and here that failure is silent:
381	// this is the fallback for a marked issue, whose title is the requester's own words,
382	// so a path that yields null leaves the item unattributable rather than rejected.
383	//
384	// It is a PARSE, not a lookup: anything that must know the task exists at HEAD
385	// resolves the path against the discovered task set instead (the executor does).
386	const PACK_TASK_PATH_RE = /^(?:\.claudinite\/shared\/)?packs\/([^/]+)\/tasks\/([^/]+)\/[^/]+$/;
387	const BUILT_IN_TASK_PATH_RE = /^(?:\.claudinite\/shared\/)?(?:engine\/scheduler|packs\/claudinite-tasks)\/queue\/tasks\/([^/]+)\/[^/]+$/;

389	export function taskIdFromPath(path) {
390	  const p = String(path ?? '');
391	  const pack = PACK_TASK_PATH_RE.exec(p);
392	  if (pack) return { pack: canonicalPackId(pack[1]), task: pack[2] };
393	  const builtIn = BUILT_IN_TASK_PATH_RE.exec(p);
394	  return builtIn ? { pack: 'engine', task: builtIn[1] } : null;
395	}

397	// STANDING OR AD-HOC, DERIVED (DESIGN §15.26). A task's standing item is the one
398	// the generator files at an anchor: its title names the task and nothing else, and
399	// the task it names is on a calendar. Everything else is ad-hoc — a `manual` task
400	// (which has no anchor to stand for) and every qualified item (a fan-out target, a
401	// request naming its issue), each of which may legitimately run beside the
402	// occurrence rather than being it.
403	//
404	// It is read off the item and the declaration at HEAD rather than off a label the
405	// creator applied, because the two could disagree: a marker says what its writer
406	// believed, the structure says what the item IS, and the guards that consume this
407	// (the occurrence guard, the dedupe, the `after` yield) are only sound on the
408	// second. `frequency` is the declared frequency of the task the title names —
409	// absent when the repo no longer carries it, which is ad-hoc by the same rule.
410	export function isStandingItem(item, frequency) {
411	  const parsed = parseWorkItemTitle(item?.title ?? item);
412	  return !!parsed && parsed.qualifier === null && frequency != null && frequency !== 'manual';

464	// hands to the policy engine (merge-policy.mjs) — `anything`, a `a;b;reject:c`
465	// rule list, or the legacy `if-narrow` (the narrow-diff composite). The run may
466	// land its own pull request only on that engine's yes, and must park for
467	// approval otherwise. An absent field is the default — never merge — so an item
468	// an older scheduler run wrote reads as unauthorized rather than as authorized.
469	export const MERGE_FIELD = 'Merge';
470	// The field's one pre-policy value, still the canonical spelling the legacy
471	// `yes`/`true` aliases collapse to on their way in.
472	export const MERGE_IF_NARROW = 'if-narrow';
473	
474	// A Merge/Automerge field value, fenced to what the policy engine can read: the
475	// canonical expression, or null for anything else. Fencing here is about SHAPE
476	// only — a well-formed policy naming a rule nobody defines rides through and
477	// fails closed at the verdict, loudly, which is better feedback than silently
478	// ignoring the ask. A policy of `nothing` is the default already, so it reads
479	// as absent.
480	//
481	// The grammar mirrors merge-policy.mjs's normalizePolicy — the semantic
482	// authority — and cannot import it: this module is deliberately pure (see the
483	// header), so the drift guard is the test that runs a value matrix through both
484	// sides (test/queue/request-mode.test.mjs).
485	const RULE_NAME = /^[a-z0-9]+(-[a-z0-9]+)*$/;
486	const PATH_SEGMENT = /^[A-Za-z0-9._-]+$/;
487	const policyName = (name) => {
488	  if (!name.startsWith('under:')) return RULE_NAME.test(name);
489	  const segments = name.slice('under:'.length).replace(/\/+$/, '').split('/');
490	  return segments.every((seg) => PATH_SEGMENT.test(seg) && seg !== '.' && seg !== '..');
491	};
492	// A term is `&&`-joined names, optionally reject:-prefixed. The value is returned
493	// CANONICAL — whitespace around `&&` collapsed — so an item body, and the trailer
494	// stamped from it, stay whitespace-free whatever a person typed.
495	function policyFieldValue(raw) {
496	  if (raw == null) return null;
497	  const value = String(raw).trim();
498	  if (['if-narrow', 'yes', 'true'].includes(value.toLowerCase())) return MERGE_IF_NARROW;
499	  if (value.toLowerCase() === 'anything') return 'anything';
500	  const terms = value.split(';').map((term) => {
501	    const prefix = term.trim().startsWith('reject:') ? 'reject:' : '';
502	    const names = term.trim().slice(prefix.length).split('&&').map((n) => n.trim());
503	    return { prefix, names, canonical: prefix + names.join('&&') };
504	  });
505	  const wellFormed = terms.length > 0
506	    && terms.every(({ names }) => names.every((n) => policyName(n) && n !== 'nothing'))
507	    && terms.some(({ prefix }) => !prefix);
508	  return wellFormed ? terms.map((t) => t.canonical).join(';') : null;
509	}
510	
511	// The heading the delivered-artifacts section carries in a work item body. One
512	// home, because it is written in three places and MATCHED when a re-entrant run
513	// updates the section it already wrote.
514	export const DELIVERED_HEADING = 'Delivered by code-work';
515	
516	// The same heading as earlier renames spelled it. A live item's body still carries
517	// whichever word was current when its section was first written, and matching only
518	// today's would append a SECOND section rather than updating that one.
519	export const LEGACY_DELIVERED_HEADINGS = Object.freeze([
520	  'Delivered by prework',
521	  'Delivered by code_work',
522	]);
523	
524	// --- the machine block (DESIGN §16.1, §16.3) ----------------------------------
525	// A one-issue request's item IS the issue somebody marked, so the item's fields
526	// share a body a person authored and keeps editing. They live in one delimited
527	// block, appended at adoption and rewritten in place after that: everything outside
528	// it belongs to the human, everything inside it to the machine, and a parser that
529	// read the whole body would take a sentence of prose for a field.
530	//
531	// A `[claudinite-work]` item has no block — its whole body is the machine's — so
532	// every reader here falls back to the whole text, which is what keeps items filed
533	// before the one-issue model draining unchanged.
534	export const MACHINE_BLOCK_START = '<!-- claudinite-item -->';
535	export const MACHINE_BLOCK_END = '<!-- /claudinite-item -->';
536	
537	const BLOCK_RE = /<!-- claudinite-item -->\n?([\s\S]*?)\n?<!-- \/claudinite-item -->/;
538	
539	// The machine's half of a body, or null where there is no block at all.
540	export const machineBlockOf = (body) => BLOCK_RE.exec(String(body ?? ''))?.[1] ?? null;
541	
542	// The machine's half to read fields out of: the block where there is one, the whole
543	// body otherwise.
544	export const itemFieldText = (body) => machineBlockOf(body) ?? String(body ?? '');
545	
546	// Replace the block, or append one to a body that has none. The human's text is
547	// never rewritten — an append lands after it, separated by a blank line.
548	export function withMachineBlock(body, block) {
549	  const text = String(body ?? '');
550	  const wrapped = `${MACHINE_BLOCK_START}\n${block.replace(/\s*$/, '')}\n${MACHINE_BLOCK_END}`;
551	  if (BLOCK_RE.test(text)) return text.replace(BLOCK_RE, wrapped);
552	  return `${text.replace(/\s*$/, '')}\n\n${wrapped}\n`;
553	}
554	
555	// Apply an edit to whichever half is the machine's. Every writer that reshapes an
556	// item body — a Context section, code-work's delivered list, a stamped
557	// `Not-before` — goes through here, so it edits the block on a marked issue and the
558	// whole body on a `[claudinite-work]` item, with one call site either way.
559	export function editItemBody(body, edit) {
560	  const block = machineBlockOf(body);
561	  return block === null ? edit(String(body ?? '')) : withMachineBlock(body, edit(block));
562	}
563	
564	// The human's half of a body — everything the machine block is not. A marked
565	// issue's PARAMETERS are read from here and never from the block: re-asking clears
566	// the status and leaves the previous run's block standing, and a parser that read
567	// the whole body would find that stale copy beside the person's own field.
568	export const humanTextOf = (body) => String(body ?? '').replace(BLOCK_RE, '').trim();
569	
570	const NOT_BEFORE_RE = /^Not-before:[ \t]*(.*)$/m;
571	const BLOCKED_BY_RE = /^Blocked-by:[ \t]*(.*)$/m;
572	const REQUEST_RE = /^Request:[ \t]*#?(\d+)/m;
573	const MODEL_RE = /^Model:[ \t]*(\S+)/m;
574	const MERGE_RE = /^Merge:[ \t]*(\S+)/m;
575	const ENDS_WHEN_RE = /^Ends-when:[ \t]*#(\d+)[ \t]+(\S+)[ \t]*$/m;
576	
577	// Build a work item body. The first line is the task path — the only thing an
578	// executor reads to locate the worker, validated in code before anything trusts
579	// it. Everything behavior-defining (model, ceiling, worker content, code-work
580	// command) is read from the tracked task files at HEAD, never from here.
581	export function workItemBody({
582	  taskPath, notBefore = null, blockedBy = [], context = [], delivered = [], reason = null,
583	  request = null, model = null, merge = null,
584	}) {
585	  const lines = [taskPath, ''];
586	  const fields = [];
587	  if (notBefore) fields.push(`${NOT_BEFORE_FIELD}: ${notBefore}`);
588	  if (blockedBy.length) fields.push(`${BLOCKED_BY_FIELD}: ${blockedBy.map((n) => `#${n}`).join(', ')}`);
589	  if (request) fields.push(`${REQUEST_FIELD}: #${request}`);
590	  if (model) fields.push(`${MODEL_FIELD}: ${model}`);
591	  if (merge) fields.push(`${MERGE_FIELD}: ${merge}`);
592	  if (fields.length) lines.push(...fields, '');
593	  lines.push('Execute the Claudinite task above.');
594	  if (context.length) {
595	    lines.push(
596	      'The Context section below is binding scope — do not re-decide it.',
597	      '',
598	      '### Context',
599	      ...context.map((c) => `- ${c}`),
600	    );
601	  }
602	  if (reason) lines.push('', '### Why the agent is here', '', `- ${reason}`);
603	  if (delivered.length) lines.push('', `### ${DELIVERED_HEADING}`, '', ...delivered.map((d) => `- ${d}`));
604	  return lines.join('\n') + '\n';
605	}
606	
607	// The `Blocked-by` numbers a body names, from a work item's body or from an
608	// ORDINARY issue's — a request marked for implementation states what it waits on in
609	// the same field spelling, and adoption carries it onto the item it births (§16.11).
610	export function parseBlockedBy(body) {
611	  const bb = BLOCKED_BY_RE.exec(String(body ?? ''))?.[1] ?? '';
612	  return [...bb.matchAll(/#(\d+)/g)].map((m) => Number(m[1]));
613	}
614	
615	// Parse an item body back into the facts the scheduler run and the executor read. A body
616	// with no first line, or whose fields are absent, yields nulls — absence is
617	// meaningful everywhere here and is never filled in with a default.
618	export function parseWorkItemBody(body) {
619	  const text = itemFieldText(body);
620	  const taskPath = text.split('\n').map((l) => l.trim()).find((l) => l !== '') ?? null;
621	  const nb = NOT_BEFORE_RE.exec(text)?.[1]?.trim() || null;
622	  const blockedBy = parseBlockedBy(text);
623	  const request = REQUEST_RE.exec(text) ? Number(REQUEST_RE.exec(text)[1]) : null;
624	  // An unrecognised family reads as absent rather than as itself: the item's model
625	  // is behaviour-defining, so the only values that leave this parser are ones the
626	  // engine can actually dispatch at (§16.7).
627	  const askedModel = MODEL_RE.exec(text)?.[1] ?? null;
628	  const model = REQUEST_MODELS.includes(askedModel) ? askedModel : null;
629	  // Same fencing as the model: an authorization that does not read as a policy
630	  // expression reads as absent, and absent is the safe end of this field — a run
631	  // that cannot read its permission opens a pull request and waits.
632	  const merge = policyFieldValue(MERGE_RE.exec(text)?.[1] ?? null);
633	  // Same fencing again, and here it is what keeps the janitor honest: a condition
634	  // it cannot evaluate must read as "no end condition", never as one that is met.
635	  const ends = ENDS_WHEN_RE.exec(text);
636	  const endsWhen = ends && ends[2] === ENDS_WHEN_CLOSED ? Number(ends[1]) : null;
637	  return { taskPath, notBefore: nb, blockedBy, request, model, merge, endsWhen };
638	}
639	
640	// WHAT A MARKED ISSUE ASKS FOR (DESIGN §16.3, §16.7, §16.11) — read from the
641	// person's own text at every adoption, so each ask names its parameters afresh and
642	// nothing stale outranks a new one.
643	//
644	// Whoever files the issue puts these on its FIRST LINES, as one block ahead of the
645	// prose — `basics/skills/do-later/SKILL.md` is where that placement is prescribed and
646	// argued. The parser does not care where they sit; a person editing the issue, and a
647	// retry rewriting `Not-before`, do.
648	//
649	// `gated` is whether the issue's AUTHOR holds push access. A body is editable by
650	// whoever opened the issue where a label was write-gated by the platform, so the
651	// three behaviour-defining fields are honoured only for an author who could have
652	// applied them as labels anyway; an ungated ask still runs, at the default task and
653	// model and with no authorization to land anything.
654	export function parseRequestFields(body, { gated = false } = {}) {
655	  const text = humanTextOf(body);
656	  const asked = {
657	    task: /^Task:[ \t]*(\S+)/m.exec(text)?.[1] ?? null,
658	    model: MODEL_RE.exec(text)?.[1] ?? null,
659	    automerge: /^Automerge:[ \t]*(.+?)[ \t]*$/m.exec(text)?.[1] ?? null,
660	  };
661	  const blockedBy = parseBlockedBy(text);
662	  const notBefore = NOT_BEFORE_RE.exec(text)?.[1]?.trim() || null;
663	  if (!gated) return { task: null, model: null, merge: null, blockedBy, notBefore, ungated: Object.values(asked).some(Boolean) };
664	  return {
665	    task: /^[^/\s]+\/[^/\s]+$/.test(asked.task ?? '') ? asked.task : null,
666	    // An unrecognised family reads as absent rather than failing the request: a run
667	    // nobody can start would look accepted forever.
668	    model: REQUEST_MODELS.includes(asked.model) ? asked.model : null,
669	    merge: policyFieldValue(asked.automerge),
670	    blockedBy,
671	    notBefore,
672	    ungated: false,
673	  };
674	}
675	
676	// The item's own `### Context` bullets, in order — the binding scope a hand-created
677	// item was born with. Read back rather than kept only for the agent to read,
678	// because an operator's PARAMETERS ride here: `create-work-item --context
679	// "REPOS=Alpha Beta"` is how a forced run says what it is running on, and the
680	// executor hands these lines to code-work as `CLAUDINITE_CONTEXT`.
681	//
682	// A section runs to the next `### ` heading or to the end of the body — the same
683	// bounds `withSection` writes to — and only `- ` bullets count, so the prose
684	// framing around a section contributes nothing.
685	function sectionLines(body, heading) {
686	  const lines = String(body ?? '').split('\n');
687	  const at = lines.findIndex((l) => l.trim() === `### ${heading}`);
688	  if (at === -1) return [];
689	  const out = [];
690	  for (const line of lines.slice(at + 1)) {
691	    if (line.startsWith('### ')) break;
692	    const m = /^-[ \t]+(.*)$/.exec(line);
693	    if (m) out.push(m[1].trim());
694	  }
695	  return out;
696	}
697	
698	export const parseContextLines = (body) => sectionLines(body, 'Context');
699	
700	// --- the roll's record ----------------------------------------------------------
701	
702	// The section a no-go roll keeps on the item: the last declined reason and the next
703	// wake, REPLACED on every roll (the item is a status line, not a log — the timeline
704	// carries the history). Serializer and parser live together so the shape has one
705	// home; the executor writes it, and anything answering "why didn't it run" — the
706	// dashboard above all — reads it back.
707	export const LAST_VERDICT_HEADING = 'Last verdict';
708	
709	export function lastVerdictLines({ at, reason, until }) {
710	  const lines = [`${at} — the precondition declined: ${reason}`];
711	  if (until) lines.push(`Asked again at ${until}.`);
712	  return lines;
713	}
714	
715	export function parseLastVerdict(body) {
716	  const lines = sectionLines(body, LAST_VERDICT_HEADING);
717	  // The reason may carry the separator itself, so the split is on the FIRST match.
718	  const first = /^(.*?) — the precondition declined: ([\s\S]*)$/.exec(lines[0] ?? '');
719	  if (!first) return null;
720	  const until = lines.map((l) => /^Asked again at (.*?)\.?$/.exec(l)).find(Boolean)?.[1] ?? null;
721	  return { at: first[1], reason: first[2], until };
722	}
723	
724	// Fold a second set of Context lines into the first, keeping order and dropping
725	// exact duplicates. Both sides are real scope — the item carries what its creator
726	// bound it to, the precondition adds what this occurrence found — and a set-write
727	// from either side would drop the other's.
728	export const mergeContext = (...groups) => [...new Set(groups.flat().filter((l) => l && l.trim()))];
729	
730	// Stamp (or clear) `Not-before` on an existing body, in place where the field is
731	// already present and directly under the task path otherwise. Text surgery rather
732	// than a rebuild: the body also carries the creating precondition's Context and
733	// code-work's Delivered section, which belong to whoever wrote them.
734	export function withNotBefore(body, iso) {
735	  const text = String(body ?? '');
736	  if (NOT_BEFORE_RE.test(text)) {
737	    return iso
738	      ? text.replace(NOT_BEFORE_RE, `${NOT_BEFORE_FIELD}: ${iso}`)
739	      : text.replace(/^Not-before:[ \t]*.*\n?/m, '');
740	  }
741	  if (!iso) return text;
742	  const lines = text.split('\n');
743	  const at = lines.findIndex((l) => l.trim() !== '');
744	  if (at === -1) return `${NOT_BEFORE_FIELD}: ${iso}\n`;
745	  lines.splice(at + 1, 0, '', `${NOT_BEFORE_FIELD}: ${iso}`);
746	  return lines.join('\n');
747	}
748	
749	// Stamp `Ends-when` on an existing body, same text surgery as `withNotBefore` and
750	// for the same reason: the body carries sections that belong to whoever wrote them.
751	// Re-stamping replaces the condition rather than adding a second one — a converge
752	// that runs twice on one item must not leave two ends.
753	export function withEndsWhen(body, number) {
754	  const text = String(body ?? '');
755	  const field = `${ENDS_WHEN_FIELD}: #${number} ${ENDS_WHEN_CLOSED}`;
756	  if (ENDS_WHEN_RE.test(text)) return text.replace(ENDS_WHEN_RE, field);
757	  const lines = text.split('\n');
758	  const at = lines.findIndex((l) => l.trim() !== '');
759	  if (at === -1) return `${field}\n`;
760	  lines.splice(at + 1, 0, '', field);
761	  return lines.join('\n');
762	}
763	
764	// Set a section of an item body (the Context, code-work's Delivered, the agent's Why)
765	// — replacing one of the same heading if it is already there, appending otherwise.
766	//
767	// REPLACING IS THE WHOLE POINT, and appending was a live bug (#879). Every standing
768	// item is born carrying a `### Context`, and the hand-off writes Context again — so
769	// an append leaves TWO sections of that name, while the session is told to read "the
770	// issue's Context section", singular. The one it reads first is then the scheduler run's birth
771	// note and the binding scope is in the other, which fails silently whichever section
772	// the agent picks. It also grows: an item re-queued through hand-off twice carried a
773	// third.
774	//
775	// A section runs to the next `### ` heading or to the end of the body, so a replaced
776	// section keeps its position rather than migrating to the bottom — the body stays in
777	// the order a reader learned it.
778	// `aliases` are older spellings of the SAME heading. The section is rewritten under
779	// `heading`, but located by any of them, so a body written before a rename is updated
780	// in place instead of gaining a second section.
781	export function withSection(body, heading, lines, aliases = []) {
782	  if (!lines.length) return body;
783	  const text = String(body ?? '').replace(/\s*$/, '');
784	  const section = [`### ${heading}`, '', ...lines.map((l) => `- ${l}`)];
785	  const existing = text.split('\n');
786	  const wanted = new Set([heading, ...aliases].map((h) => `### ${h}`));
787	  const at = existing.findIndex((l) => wanted.has(l.trim()));
788	  if (at === -1) return `${text}\n\n${section.join('\n')}\n`;
789	  const after = existing.findIndex((l, i) => i > at && l.startsWith('### '));
790	  const tail = after === -1 ? [] : ['', ...existing.slice(after)];
791	  return `${[...existing.slice(0, at), ...section, ...tail].join('\n')}\n`;
792	}

1	// THE OPERATOR HOLD (tasks-dispatch DESIGN §8, decision §15.24). One repository
2	// Actions variable stops the whole queue: every Claudinite workflow stamps it
3	// into its env, and every engine entry point checks it as its FIRST act — before
4	// any read, like the dormancy gate beside it — and exits cleanly having fired
5	// nothing.
6	//
7	// Why a variable rather than a commit: cancelling one run means "move on", an
8	// intent the failure continuation and the leash already serve. Stopping the
9	// SYSTEM is a different intent, and the only lever that existed for it was
10	// dormancy, which needs a commit and a converge to take effect and another to
11	// undo. A variable takes effect on the next run and clears the same way.
12	//
13	// What it freezes: STARTS, and — since the drain became batched (§15.30) — each
14	// PICK inside a running drain. A run already past this gate finishes the item it
15	// holds: killing live work would leave exactly the half-done state the leash
16	// exists to recover. Nothing NEW is ever picked.
17	//
18	// Resume needs no code: clear the variable and the next scheduler run reclaims, readies and
19	// drains on its own. The impatient path is dispatching the SCHEDULER workflow, not
20	// the bare executor — the scheduler run is what re-derives the world.
21	
22	export const SUSPEND_ALL_VAR = 'CLAUDINITE_TASKS_SUSPEND_ALL';
23	
24	// Deliberately narrow: a variable somebody set to `false` or `0` to mean "off"
25	// must not read as on. Anything else — unset, empty, a word — is not a hold.
26	export const isSuspended = (env = process.env) =>
27	  ['true', '1', 'yes'].includes(String(env[SUSPEND_ALL_VAR] ?? '').trim().toLowerCase());
28	
29	// THE BETWEEN-ITEMS READ (§15.30). `vars.*` reaches a run's env at START only, so
30	// a batched drain — which may legally run for hours — cannot see a hold set after
31	// it began by re-reading its own environment. This asks the API instead, once per
32	// item boundary.
33	//
34	// A read that does not answer is NOT a verdict. It falls back to the value this
35	// run started with and SAYS which path it took: a hold silently reading as "off"
36	// spends the queue the operator was stopping, and one silently reading as "on"
37	// freezes a queue nobody held. The fallback is also what the run degrades to
38	// where the token cannot read repository variables at all — the hold then reaches
39	// this drain only when it next starts, exactly as it did before the drain
40	// batched, and every boundary says so rather than looking like a live check.
41	export async function readSuspendedNow(gh, repo, { env = process.env, log = () => {} } = {}) {
42	  const { status, json } = await gh(`/repos/${repo}/actions/variables/${SUSPEND_ALL_VAR}`);
43	  // Parsed by the same predicate as the env copy: two spellings of "is this on"
44	  // would eventually disagree, and this one decides whether work stops.
45	  if (status === 200) return isSuspended({ [SUSPEND_ALL_VAR]: json?.value });
46	  // Not set is not a fault: the variable simply does not exist, which is the
47	  // normal state of every repo nobody has ever held.
48	  if (status === 404) return false;
49	  log(`! could not read ${SUSPEND_ALL_VAR} live (${status}) — using the value this run started with.`
50	    + ' Reading a repository variable needs a token with variables read access; without it a hold'
51	    + ' reaches a running drain only when its next run starts.');
52	  return isSuspended(env);
53	}
54	
55	// The one line every entry point prints when it parks, so a run that did nothing
56	// says WHY it did nothing — a silent clean exit is indistinguishable from a run
57	// that found no work.
58	export const suspendedNotice = () =>
59	  `- ${SUSPEND_ALL_VAR} is set: the queue is held. Nothing is picked up, created, readied or reclaimed.\n`
60	  + '  Clear the variable in repo settings (Settings → Secrets and variables → Actions → Variables) to resume;'
61	  + ' the next scheduled scheduler run recovers everything on its own.';

1	// basics task: task-janitor — the THIRD responsibility of the scheduled-task
2	// machinery (owner, 2026-08-06). The scheduler run CREATES and readies work items, the
3	// executor EXECUTES exactly the one item it picked, and this task — alone —
4	// cleans up after both: items stuck ready past their period, items left wearing
5	// no state label by a torn transition, and a health review of the open set.
6	// Neither the scheduler run nor the executor does any of that; a task execution cares only
7	// about its own item, and recovery lives here, in code, once a day.
8	//
9	// It also sweeps what the retired slot mechanism left behind: the last slot runs
10	// filed `[claudinite-task]` dispatch issues in members, and nothing else closes
11	// them out. That half retires when the fleet's are gone, not before.
12	//
13	// The scheduler run reclaims a dead executor claim itself, hourly — this task is the
14	// slower backstop for what the scheduler run's deterministic label mechanics cannot see.
15	//
16	// `agent_model: 'none'` + code_work: the whole pass is deterministic code the
17	// executor runs as code-work — no agent phase, fully automatic.
18	//
19	// Self-contained (imports nothing): the whole contract is this default export.
20	
21	export default {
22	  id: 'task-janitor',
23	  frequency: 'daily',
24	  precondition_signals: [],
25	  agent_model: 'none',                   // pure code — cleanup needs no judgment
26	  expected_outcome: 'none',              // labels and comments only, never a PR
27	  code_work: 'node worker.mjs',
28	  // One repo-wide issue search plus a handful of label/comment writes — seconds.
29	  code_work_timeout: 300,
30	
31	  // Unconditional, and honestly so: the sweep itself is the cheap way to learn
32	  // whether anything needs cleaning, and a quiet repo costs one search. The
33	  // precondition is the ONLY decision point in a task's life — this one simply
34	  // always decides yes.
35	  precondition() {
36	    return { run: true, reason: 'daily dispatch-issue cleanup and health review' };
37	  },
38	};

input.title: Coded production validations: declarative URL probes a code worker fetches and judges
input.body:
The verify-in-production lane's only runner is an agentic session, which has no egress — so a verification whose artifact is a live URL (a Pages site, a deployed config) cannot run at all. #1184 and #1288 were filed exactly that way and parked `needs-human` minutes after being picked; the skill's current answer is "file nothing", which leaves every live-site change permanently unverified.

Requirement: a **coded** validation form beside the agentic one.

- The verification issue carries declarative probes on its first lines: `Live-probe:` / `Verify-probe:` lines, each `<url> :: <assertion>` (status / contains / matches / JSON-value queries).
- An agentless queue task (`Task:`-routed, `agent_model: none`) runs them as code-work — Action-side, where egress exists.
- Any liveness probe failing → not yet live: re-arm `Not-before:` to now + `Retry-every:` and leave the item open (a new code-work → executor requeue protocol; today a code worker can only close done or park).
- Liveness passing but a verify probe failing → reopen `Original-issue:` with what was asserted and what was read; the verification did its job.
- All passing → close done with the evidence actually fetched.

Loop closing: the validation is forceable at filing time (`create-work-item --wake` / the scheduler's wake input), so the filer watches it run and report **not yet live** before the feature ships — the probes are proven against the real machinery, then flip on their own once the release lands.

# verify-production — coded production validations

The queue's coded verification lane (#1530). A change whose proof lives at a URL — a
Pages site, a deployed config, a published module — cannot be verified by an agent
session, which has no egress. This task is the runner for those: the verification
issue carries declarative probes, and the worker fetches and judges them as
code-work, Action-side, where egress exists.

The filing form — when to file one at all, and the brief's fields — is the basics
pack's [verify-in-production](../../../basics/skills/verify-in-production/SKILL.md)
skill. An issue routes here by naming `Task: claudinite-tasks/verify-production`
beside its mark.

## The spec the worker reads

Parsed from the human half of the issue body by [`probes.mjs`](probes.mjs), which
is also where the assertion grammar is defined and documented:

```
Original-issue: #<n>
Task: claudinite-tasks/verify-production
Live-probe: <url> :: <assertion>
Verify-probe: <url> :: <assertion>
Retry-every: <count> <minutes|hours|days|weeks>
```

Both probe classes are required, and the difference is the whole design: a failing
`Live-probe:` means the release has not landed (re-arm and come back), a failing
`Verify-probe:` — judged only once liveness passes — means a real fault in
production. Without the gate the two are indistinguishable, and a verify failure
would reopen the original issue over a release that simply has not happened.

## The four verdicts

- **invalid** — the spec is unreadable: the worker exits non-zero with a triage
  marker naming every problem, and the item parks.
- **not yet live** — the worker prints the `claudinite-requeue:` marker with
  now + `Retry-every:` and exits clean; the executor re-arms the item's
  `Not-before` and returns it to blocked.
- **pass** — the evidence actually read is commented on the item; the executor
  closes it done.
- **fail** — `Original-issue:` is reopened with what was asserted and what was
  read; the item links it and closes done — the verification did its job by
  finding the fault.

## Watching a fresh one fail

A coded run costs seconds, so a new verification should be watched failing before
its release lands: dispatch the scheduler workflow (its `workflow_dispatch`), and
the adoption-plus-drain executes the probes immediately. The run reporting
**not yet live** is the see-it-fail proof — the probes execute and do not pass
vacuously — and the same item then flips on its own once the release is live.

# claudinite-tasks — scheduled work

Everything whose subject is task work: the work-item queue, the executor, the task contract and
its signals, calendar/anchor math, run records, code-work, and the delivery lane a task's output
lands through. Declaring this pack is what gives a repo scheduled work; a repo that does not
declare it runs none, which is a supported state rather than a degraded one.

The mechanism itself — the state machine, the generator, the executor's protocol, urgency and
forcing, recovery — is the canon's own tasks-dispatch design document, and authoring a task is the
`writing-tasks` skill's subject. This file is the pack's own map.

## Layout

| Path | What lives there |
|---|---|
| `queue/` | the work item and its vocabulary, the scheduler run, the executor and its continuation, the drain, leases, readiness, the janitor's rules, the schedule board, workflow-failure escalation |
| `queue/tasks/` | the built-in tasks (`implement-request`) |
| `signals/` | the signal collectors a precondition is handed |
| `stubs/` | the two workflow files an adopting repo receives |
| `shared-code/` | the published import surface — see below |
| `tasks/` | this pack's own scheduled tasks: `task-janitor` (the queue's sweeps) and `usage-fold` (it folds this mechanism's run records and outcome labels) |
| `worldRules/` | the task-declaration checks |
| `workRules/` | the armed-auto-merge gate (`automerge-policy-scope`) |
| `merge-policy.mjs` | the auto-merge policy engine: what a task's `automerge`, an item's `Merge:` field and the arming trailer mean, the built-in diff classes, the inline `under:<dir>` folder scope, the `&&` intersection, and the `merge-rules.json` vocabulary a pack extends them with |
| `test/` | the unit suite, and `test/sim/` — the simulator and its scenario suite, the mechanism's executable spec |
| `executor.md`, `queue/instructions.md`, `deliver-pr.md` | operational documents a member's routines and workers read out of their own mount at runtime |

## `shared-code/` — the one sanctioned cross-pack import

Another pack's code may import `packs/claudinite-tasks/shared-code/*`, and nothing else of this
pack. The `pack-independence` barrier's allow list names that directory; no other pack gains an
equivalent surface by existing.

| Module | What it publishes | Who reads it |
|---|---|---|
| `work-items.mjs` | the title grammar that is a work item's identity, the outcome/status decode over its labels, lease state, the dispatch vocabulary, and what a scheduler run would instantiate | claudinite-dashboard, claudinite-fleet-sheepdog |
| `anchors.mjs` | period length, and the instant a task's window last opened at or opens next | claudinite-dashboard |
| `delivery.mjs` | `landPr`, `deliverGenerated` — how a task's output becomes a landed PR or a regenerated file | any pack whose tasks deliver |
| `github.mjs` | the GitHub client and REST helpers, and the tracker issue a worker records on | any pack whose tasks reach GitHub |
| `signals.mjs` | the signal shapes a precondition is handed | packs asserting what their own tasks will see |
| `task-contract.mjs` | task-declaration validation, and precondition evaluation as the executor does it | every pack with tasks, in its own tests |
| `merge-policy.mjs` | the auto-merge policy verdict (`automerge`, the `Merge:` field, the arming trailer) and the `merge-rules.json` compiler | any pack declaring policies or merge rules, in its own tests |
| `usage-format.mjs` | the usage aggregate's codec | claudinite-fleet-sheepdog's fleet-wide aggregator |

A pack whose **non-task** code reads any of these declares `requires: ['claudinite-tasks']`. A
pack's `tasks/` folder needs no declaration: a mount without this pack carries no `tasks/` at all,
since a task folder is inert without the queue that runs it.

## Adoption

The two workflow files and the routine endpoints cannot converge into place — `.github/workflows/`
is the one directory a member's nightly update may never write — so they are scaffolded once, at
adoption, by the `adopt-pack` skill. They are static from then on: the per-repo cron minute and
anchor hours are written once, secrets travel as one fixed line, and the `run:` lines name mount
pack paths behind which everything converges nightly.

## The legacy `engine/scheduler/` shims

Until #1317's execution chain finishes, `engine/scheduler/*` still exists as one-line re-exports of
this pack, for members whose vendored workers, workflow `run:` lines and stored routine prompts
still name the old paths. They ship only into a mount that carries this pack, and they are deleted
once no fielded member names one.

## Checks

| Rule | Confidence | Dimension | Enforcement |
|---|---|---|---|
| `task-declaration-shape` | high | correctness | check: blocking |
| `task-code-work-env` | high | correctness | check: blocking |
| `automerge-policy-scope` | high | correctness | check: blocking |

The first two are relevance-first — inert until the repo carries a `tasks/<name>/task.mjs` of its own; the third is self-gating on the branch's own arming trailer.

- `task-declaration-shape` — a task declaration the scheduler reads is incomplete or illegal, so the task never fires or fires wrong.
- `task-code-work-env` — a task reads a `CLAUDINITE_*` variable code-work never sets, so a parameter (a scope filter, a dry-run switch) silently never arrives and the run goes green in its most dangerous mode.
- `automerge-policy-scope` — a branch that stamped the `Claudinite-Automerge-Policy` trailer (its run intends to land its own PR) carries a diff its declared policy does not cover, which is exactly the unreviewed change the policy exists to stop.

input.old_string:
## Second: can the RUN read it? If not, file nothing

The run is an unattended session on this repository, and its reach is narrower than
yours: **GitHub, through its own tools, in the repositories its routine's scope names**
— and nothing else. There is no browser and no general egress, so a `*.github.io` page,
a live site's `/version.json`, a console, a dashboard and a login-walled report are all
unreadable to it, and so is a repository outside that scope. **Another repo is the
standard trap**, because the read looks ordinary and the wall is invisible from here:
#1349, #1351 and #1396 each named a member repo, and each parked minutes after being
picked, on `repository "…" is not configured for this session`.

So take the read you are about to write into `Verify:` and answer, in one sentence,
*which tool call the run makes, in which repository*.
**If you cannot name one, file nothing** — say in your reply that the change is
unverified and what would prove it.
That is a filter, not a fork: an unreadable artifact is a reason not to file, and the
forms below are not two equal options. Filing anyway spends a session rediscovering the
wall and then parks `needs-human-action`, which is the human's-memory outcome this skill
exists to avoid — one executor batch spent five of its seven claimed items exactly that
way (#1184, #1253, #1268, #1288, #1291).

## Second: which runner can read it? If neither, file nothing

There are two runners, and the artifact's address decides which one a verification
gets — never preference:

- **A public URL** — a Pages site, a deployed config, a published module, a live
  `/version.json` — files the **coded form**: declarative probes an agentless queue
  task (`claudinite-tasks/verify-production`) fetches and judges Action-side, where
  egress exists. No session ever runs, so there is no egress wall to hit — this is
  the lane for exactly the class that used to park (#1184, #1288).
- **A GitHub read** — an issue's state, a file at HEAD, a workflow run's conclusion —
  files the **agentic form**: an unattended session on this repository, whose reach
  is narrower than yours — **GitHub, through its own tools, in the repositories its
  routine's scope names** — and nothing else. Take the read you are about to write
  into `Verify:` and answer, in one sentence, *which tool call the run makes, in
  which repository*. **Another repo is the standard trap**, because the read looks
  ordinary and the wall is invisible from here: #1349, #1351 and #1396 each named a
  member repo, and each parked minutes after being picked, on
  `repository "…" is not configured for this session`. A cross-repo artifact with a
  public URL — a member's stamp on `raw.githubusercontent.com`, its Pages site — is
  not walled at all: it is a URL, and the coded form reads it.
- **Neither** — a login-walled console, a private dashboard, a repository outside
  scope with no public surface — **file nothing**: say in your reply that the change
  is unverified and what would prove it. That is a filter, not a fork: an unreadable
  artifact is a reason not to file. Filing anyway spends a session rediscovering the
  wall and then parks `needs-human-action`, which is the human's-memory outcome this
  skill exists to avoid — one executor batch spent five of its seven claimed items
  exactly that way (#1184, #1253, #1268, #1288, #1291), before the coded form
  existed for the URL-readable ones among them.

input.new_string:
### The coded form — for a URL-readable artifact

```
Original-issue: #<the change's issue>
Task: claudinite-tasks/verify-production
Live-probe: <url> :: <assertion that becomes true when the release lands>
Verify-probe: <url> :: <the assertion being verified>
Retry-every: <how often to re-probe while not yet live, e.g. 6 hours>
```

The probes are the whole check, executed in code by the task the `Task:` line names —
no session, no `Model:`. `Live-probe:` is `In-production-when:` made executable and
`Verify-probe:` is `Verify:`; both classes are required, repeat either line for more
probes, and the assertion grammar (`status`, `contains`, `matches`, the `json` value
ops) is documented at its one home,
[`probes.mjs`](../../../claudinite-tasks/tasks/verify-production/probes.mjs). A
liveness probe failing re-arms the item by `Retry-every:`; a verify probe failing
against a live release reopens `Original-issue:` with what was asserted and what was
read; all passing closes the item with that evidence. No `Not-before:` is needed: a
coded run costs seconds, so probing from the moment of filing is the point, not a
waste — see the watch-it-fail step below.

### The agentic form — for a GitHub read

```
Original-issue: #<the change's issue>
In-production-when: <the concrete artifact to read, and what makes it true>
Verify: <what to observe, and what counts as a pass>
Not-before: <ISO instant just past the expected release>
Retry-every: <how far to push Not-before when not yet live, e.g. 1 day>
Model: sonnet
```

In either form, no `Blocked-by:`. You are filing after the merge, so the change's PR has
already closed and there is nothing left to wait on but the release itself.

input.new_string:
## Then watch it fail, and say what you filed

A coded verification runs for seconds, so its first execution is not left to faith: dispatch
the scheduler workflow (its `workflow_dispatch`) and watch the first run report **not yet
live** — proof the probes execute and fail for the right reason instead of passing vacuously;
the same item then flips on its own once the release lands. A first run that *passes* before
the release you expected deserves a hard look, because a probe that cannot fail proves
nothing. The agentic form sleeps until its `Not-before:` and has no cheap forced run; filing
it correctly is the watch.

One line back to the owner: the issue link, what it waits on, and its retry cadence.

# Version history

Records for `packs/basics/pack.mjs`'s `version` field, one row per bump — added going forward from
the version this file was introduced beside (60821.4); earlier bumps are not backfilled.

| Version | Date | What changed |
|---|---|---|
| 60831.4 | 2026-08-31 | The reachability gate is a filter rather than a router: an artifact the run cannot read is a reason to file nothing and say the change is unverified, and asking a person is a rare exception earned by a costly silent failure — not the fallback whenever no automatic check exists. A fleet-wide subject belongs to a routine holding fleet scope or to nobody. The same bar reaches every ad-hoc item in `RULES.md`: a marked issue asks an unattended session on this repo to do the work, and work it cannot do here parks minutes after being picked (#1520). |
| 60831.3 | 2026-08-31 | `production-retrospective` — an element that earned a design doc or a phased tracking issue schedules the review that comes back ~a week after it works as planned, asking working / misused / overused / underused against its production record. The brief is written at design time — expected amounts, behaviours, the signals for misuse, overuse and a wrong decision, the re-examinable decisions, and the metrics the run will read (built with the element) — never improvised at run time; findings route by kind, implementation faults to task issues and disproven decisions to discussion issues parked on the owner. Filed on the ad-hoc lane as a migration chain's last link or beside `verify-in-production` at the merge; the lane is open to further classes — canon-pack, local-pack or fleet (#1501). |
| 60831.2 | 2026-08-31 | `verify-in-production`'s playbook converges through `converge-item.mjs`, which needs no REST route and is the whole path on every session — and never a `task:status:*` label written by hand, which records a pass nowhere the queue reads and then hides the item from the leash (#1499). |
| 60831.1 | 2026-08-31 | `verify-in-production` gates on what the RUN can read before filing: a GitHub read in the routine's scope gets the automatic form, and a web page, deployed site, console or dashboard gets the human-step form — an ordinary assigned issue with no mark, rather than a queue item that spends a session rediscovering the wall and parks. The "watch it now" test asks whether the artifact becomes readable inside this session, not only whether it already did (#1500). |
| 60830.6 | 2026-08-30 | `do-later` proposes an `Automerge:` policy from the folder first — a deferral's tree is known at filing time, and a folder bound holds where a repo-wide kind class does not — reaching for a bare kind only where no single tree bounds the change, and for review where several unrelated trees do (#1483). |
| 60830.5 | 2026-08-30 | `runnable-doc-commands` — a `node <path>` written in a pack doc is a command an agent will run, and nothing opens it until one does; the check judges the two shapes the corpus owns (a placeholder-rooted path by its suffix, a mount path against the canon beneath it) and leaves a consuming repo's own paths alone (#1475). |
| 60830.4 | 2026-08-30 | `do-later`'s `Automerge:` vocabulary carries the inline folder scope `under:<dir>` and the `&&` intersection, so a deferral confined to one tree — or to that tree's documents — can authorize exactly that (#1473). |
| 60830.3 | 2026-08-30 | `/do-later` must settle the automerge value: the `Automerge:` field takes a policy expression, and a deferral that names none gets one `AskUserQuestion` proposing the narrowest fitting policy, review remaining the default only after the owner had the chance to choose. `ci-performance` declares `pr`/`anything` — CI itself gates a CI-performance fix (#1459). |
| 60827.2 | 2026-08-27 | `do-later` can defer onto a *moment*: a time-worded ask ("check tomorrow") rides the queue's `Not-before:` wait field instead of falling through to "queues immediately" (#1393). |
| 60824.1 | 2026-08-24 | The `task-janitor` task moves to the new `claudinite-tasks` pack, which owns the queue it sweeps (#1317). |
| 60823.1 | 2026-08-23 | Prose and skills name the member settings file by its current name, `.claudinite-settings.json` (#1252). |
| 60822.1 | 2026-08-22 | The manifest stops restating its own tree (#1246): `id`, `prose`, `badge`, `skills`, `worldRules` and `workRules` are resolved from the pack directory and an absent `detect`/`marker` means no fingerprint. Coded rules move into `worldRules/`/`workRules/` and tests into `test/`, which no vendor set ships. `minEngineVersion` rises to the engine release that reads all of it. |
| 60827.1 | 2026-08-27 | The task-janitor's queue sweep parks with ONE label — `task:status:needs-human-<kind>` — rather than the `needs-human` pair a half-applied swap could tear (#1119). |
| 60830.1 | 2026-08-30 | The `ci-performance` brief names the park the engine writes — one `task:status:needs-human-<kind>` (#1395). |
| 60830.2 | 2026-08-30 | The ad-hoc request skills place every field a run reads as one block on the issue body's first lines, and `verify-in-production`'s retry re-arms `Not-before:` to now + `Retry-every:` rather than to the stale value plus it (#1456). |

content.subject: File the GitHub issue for coded production validations
content.description: Lifecycle step 1: an issue describing the requirement — a coded (non-agentic) production-validation lane: URL fetch + declarative query, runs Action-side where egress exists, re-arms while not-yet-live, reopens the original issue on failure.

content.subject: Add the requeue protocol to the queue engine
content.description: A code worker printing `claudinite-requeue: <ISO> — <reason>` on an ok exit makes the executor stamp Not-before (machine block) and swap running-executor → blocked instead of closing done. Reader in code-work.mjs, handling in executor.mjs; tests first, watch them fail.

content.subject: Build the verify-production task (probe grammar + worker)
content.description: packs/claudinite-tasks/tasks/verify-production/: agentless manual task; probes.mjs parses `Live-probe:`/`Verify-probe:` lines (url :: assertion — status/contains/matches/json ops) and evaluates them over injected fetch; worker.mjs reads the item's human text, runs probes, requeues when not live, comments evidence and closes on pass, reopens Original-issue on fail.

content.subject: Update the verify-in-production skill and its prose tests
content.description: The coded form becomes the preferred lane for URL-readable artifacts; the "can the RUN read it" gate gains it; the filer forces a run now and watches it report not-yet-live (see-it-fail). Keep the agentic form for GitHub-tool reads.

input.body:
Closes #1530

A verification whose artifact is a live URL — a Pages site, a deployed config — could not run at all: the queue's only runner was an agentic session, which has no egress, and #1184/#1288 parked exactly that way. This adds the **coded form**: declarative probes a code worker fetches and judges Action-side, where egress exists.

Three commits, in dependency order:

1. **The requeue protocol** (`code-work.mjs`, `queue/code-work-run.mjs`, `queue/executor.mjs`). A worker printing `claudinite-requeue: <instant> — <reason>` before a clean exit has the executor stamp the item's `Not-before` (machine half), strike its claim, and return the item to blocked — the third answer an exit code could not give (0 closes done, non-zero parks). Honoured only on an OK exit; an unreadable instant parks loudly.
2. **The `verify-production` task** (`claudinite-tasks/tasks/verify-production/`): agentless, `frequency: manual`, routed to by `Task: claudinite-tasks/verify-production` on a marked issue. `probes.mjs` is the grammar's one home — `Live-probe:`/`Verify-probe:` lines, each `<url> :: <assertion>` (`status`, `[not ]contains`, `[not ]matches`, and `json` path ops including a segment-wise-numeric `>=` for dotted version stamps). Both classes required: liveness failing → requeue by `Retry-every:`; a verify probe failing while live → reopen `Original-issue:` with what was asserted and what was read; all passing → close with the evidence.
3. **The skill** (`basics/verify-in-production`): the reachability gate becomes runner routing (URL → coded, GitHub read → agentic, neither → file nothing), with the coded template first, and a closing step that forces a scheduler run at filing time so the filer **watches the first run report not yet live** — the probes proven failing before the release lands, then flipping on their own once it does. The ad-hoc-queue rule in `basics/RULES.md` carries the matching exception.

Both packs bumped with `VERSIONS.md` rows. Suite: 2867/2867; `check_the_work` and `check_the_world` clean (the two `file-placement` advisories on `worker.mjs` are the same deliberate in-pack reach `task-janitor`'s worker stands on).

Follow-up once merged: re-file #1184 and #1288 in the coded form — both are pure URL reads (stamps, deployed configs, a published module's imports) — and watch their first runs.

content.text:
Done. The feature is built, tested and up for review as [PR #1534](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/pull/1534), closing [#1530](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/issues/1530).

**What #1184/#1288 were missing, and what now exists.** Their verifications needed to read live URLs, and the queue's only runner was an agentic session with no egress. Now a verification issue can carry declarative probes and route to a new agentless task, `claudinite-tasks/verify-production`, whose worker runs as code-work in the executor's own Actions job — which has real egress. Two probe classes with distinct failure meanings: a `Live-probe:` failing means the release hasn't landed (the item re-arms by `Retry-every:`), a `Verify-probe:` failing once liveness passes reopens `Original-issue:` with what was asserted vs. what was read. The grammar covers `status`, `contains`, `matches`, and `json` path ops — including a segment-wise `>=` so `60821.10` correctly beats `60821.3` for stamp comparisons like #1184's.

**The loop-closing you asked for** is designed in: a coded run costs seconds, so the skill's filing procedure now ends with forcing a scheduler run immediately and watching the first execution report **not yet live** — the probes proven executing and failing before the feature ships, then flipping on their own once it's live. This needed one new engine primitive: a code worker printing `claudinite-requeue: <instant> — <reason>` gets its item re-armed to blocked instead of closed done (previously exit 0 = done, non-zero = park; "come back later" had no spelling).

Docs edited: [verify-in-production SKILL.md](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/blob/claude/production-validation-coded-access-mwl16z/packs/basics/skills/verify-in-production/SKILL.md), [basics RULES.md](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/blob/claude/production-validation-coded-access-mwl16z/packs/basics/RULES.md) (the "web page is unreachable" rule now carries the coded-form exception), and the new task's [README](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/blob/claude/production-validation-coded-access-mwl16z/packs/claudinite-tasks/tasks/verify-production/README.md) / [probes.mjs](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/blob/claude/production-validation-coded-access-mwl16z/packs/claudinite-tasks/tasks/verify-production/probes.mjs).

```

packs/claudinite-tasks/                        — code-work.mjs gains the claudinite-requeue marker reader
packs/claudinite-tasks/queue/                  — executor honours the ask: stamp Not-before, strike claim, back to blocked
packs/claudinite-tasks/tasks/verify-production/ — new task: probe grammar, code worker, declaration
packs/basics/skills/verify-in-production/      — the coded form: runner routing, template, watch-it-fail step
packs/basics/                                  — RULES.md ad-hoc-queue rule: public URLs reachable via the coded form only

# Owner interaction preferences

Personal preferences from the repo owner for how the assistant should interact — tone, summary style, end-of-turn conventions, how results and decisions are surfaced, and the phrases the owner uses to trigger defined commands. These are **not** project conventions (those live in the [packs/](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/tree/main/packs) corpus, each pack bundling its skills); they're how the owner likes to be worked with. Where a preference triggers a command whose mechanics are a project convention, the mechanics stay in their own doc and the entry here just owns the trigger phrase.

## Preferences

- **End every turn with a blockquote callout** — `> ✅ All done`, or `> ⚠️ Still open: …` listing what remains — never hedged in prose.
- **"LGTM"** merges the change at hand into `main` (`merge-to-main` skill); it approves that change only, never later work.
- **"bump version"** raises the project's version; the project's own workflow decides how it changes and which files change.
- **In the conversation**: link every source-controlled document you edit, display every image you edit, link every issue/PR number.
- **Ask every decision or approval through an `AskUserQuestion` popup, never prose** — one question per item, each with its case.
- **Enclose anything the owner will lift elsewhere** — a prompt, a message, copy to paste — in one delimited block, boundaries unmistakable.
- **Prefix a prompt for another session, inside its block, with a disclaimer**: Claude wrote it — examine inconsistencies, don't follow blindly.
- **Open a pull request right after committing to a branch**, unasked — overriding Claude Code's default of waiting to be told.
- **When handing over a PR to review, describe the folders the change touched in the conversation, in a text box** — a brief line per folder saying what changed there. Show non-test folders only, and ignore README files, comment-only changes, and history-keeping updates (a version bump, a changelog or `VERSIONS.md` row).
- **Keep working through a multi-step plan without pausing for approval of each step** — aggregate the steps into one substantial change to review, and stop only for an action that reaches the world (a release, a fleet-wide effect, anything irreversible) or a decision only the owner can make.
- **Never schedule a self check-in to poll a PR** — no recurring wake-up, routine, or `send_later` re-arm that re-reads a PR's state, CI or mergeability on a timer. Act on PR events when they arrive; when nothing has arrived, end the turn.

content.text:
Claudinite loaded, 9 packs, 38 checks, 14,500 rule tokens, 23 available skills, 550 personal preference tokens.

Comment class: other
A placement question — here's the case, and I think the current placement is right.

Four grounds for `claudinite-tasks` over `basics`:

1. **It's the queue's second issue-routed runner, and the first one lives there.** `implement-request` — the task a marked issue routes to by default — is the queue pack's own ([queue/tasks/implement-request/task.mjs](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/blob/main/packs/claudinite-tasks/queue/tasks/implement-request/task.mjs)), as are `task-janitor` and `usage-fold`. `verify-production` is the same species: a runner whose whole behavior is *how the queue executes one class of item*. Basics owns the **discipline** — when a verification is filed and what the brief says (the skill) — and that split matches the packs' own routing guidance: claudinite-tasks "belongs: scheduled work — the queue, the executor, the task contract, code-work"; basics is cross-project working discipline.

2. **The protocol's emitter and reader stay in one pack.** The worker prints `claudinite-requeue:`; only the executor reads it. In one pack, the marker grammar, its emitter, and its reader change in one commit under one version, and the pack's test suite covers both halves against each other. Split across packs, the marker becomes a cross-pack wire protocol — a compatibility surface to hold open forever, for no gain.

3. **Pack independence.** The worker reads the item's body through the queue's own vocabulary (`humanTextOf`, the machine-block split, [queue/work-item.mjs](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/blob/main/packs/claudinite-tasks/queue/work-item.mjs)). Inside claudinite-tasks that's an ordinary in-pack import. From basics it would have to squeeze through `shared-code/` for everything it needs, or duplicate — and the repo's standing rule is that packs don't depend on each other beyond that one sanctioned surface.

4. **The task exists exactly where the queue exists.** A task is discovered only from a declared pack. Hosted in basics, a repo could carry the task with no executor to run it (basics declared, claudinite-tasks not); hosted in the queue pack, the runner and the machinery that routes to it are declared, vendored, and versioned as one unit.

The one cost of the current placement is cosmetic: the skill (basics) names `Task: claudinite-tasks/verify-production` across a pack boundary. But that coupling is inherent — the skill's entire queue lane already presumes the queue pack, whichever pack hosts the worker. And note the id is about to become stored data (written into verification issues), so wherever it lives at merge is effectively permanent — moving later costs a decode-side rename. I'd keep it where it is.

> ✅ All done — assessment only, nothing changed. Still open: [PR #1534](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/pull/1534) awaits review ("LGTM" merges).

# Owner interaction preferences

Personal preferences from the repo owner for how the assistant should interact — tone, summary style, end-of-turn conventions, how results and decisions are surfaced, and the phrases the owner uses to trigger defined commands. These are **not** project conventions (those live in the [packs/](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/tree/main/packs) corpus, each pack bundling its skills); they're how the owner likes to be worked with. Where a preference triggers a command whose mechanics are a project convention, the mechanics stay in their own doc and the entry here just owns the trigger phrase.

## Preferences

- **End every turn with a blockquote callout** — `> ✅ All done`, or `> ⚠️ Still open: …` listing what remains — never hedged in prose.
- **"LGTM"** merges the change at hand into `main` (`merge-to-main` skill); it approves that change only, never later work.
- **"bump version"** raises the project's version; the project's own workflow decides how it changes and which files change.
- **In the conversation**: link every source-controlled document you edit, display every image you edit, link every issue/PR number.
- **Ask every decision or approval through an `AskUserQuestion` popup, never prose** — one question per item, each with its case.
- **Enclose anything the owner will lift elsewhere** — a prompt, a message, copy to paste — in one delimited block, boundaries unmistakable.
- **Prefix a prompt for another session, inside its block, with a disclaimer**: Claude wrote it — examine inconsistencies, don't follow blindly.
- **Open a pull request right after committing to a branch**, unasked — overriding Claude Code's default of waiting to be told.
- **When handing over a PR to review, describe the folders the change touched in the conversation, in a text box** — a brief line per folder saying what changed there. Show non-test folders only, and ignore README files, comment-only changes, and history-keeping updates (a version bump, a changelog or `VERSIONS.md` row).
- **Keep working through a multi-step plan without pausing for approval of each step** — aggregate the steps into one substantial change to review, and stop only for an action that reaches the world (a release, a fleet-wide effect, anything irreversible) or a decision only the owner can make.
- **Never schedule a self check-in to poll a PR** — no recurring wake-up, routine, or `send_later` re-arm that re-reads a PR's state, CI or mergeability on a timer. Act on PR events when they arrive; when nothing has arrived, end the turn.

---
name: merge-to-main
description: Merge the change in front of the owner into main. Use when the owner says "LGTM" or asks to merge/land the current branch or PR into main.
---

# Merge to main

If the project's own `CLAUDE.md` names a merge-policy file, that file overrides the divergent
points below (merge method, CI gating). Don't go hunting for one it doesn't name.

1. Load `create_pull_request` + `merge_pull_request` in one `ToolSearch`.
2. No PR open for the branch? `create_pull_request` (base `main`), body ending `Closes #<issue>`.
3. If the PR has check runs, wait for them to pass. None — merge without waiting.
4. `merge_pull_request`, `merge_method: squash`, title `<subject> (#<pr>)`. Don't pre-read
   mergeability; the call fails loudly.
5. Sync local `main`: `git checkout main && git pull origin main`.
6. Capture the conversation:
   `node .claudinite/shared/packs/claudinite-growth/capture-log.mjs --issue <n>`
   (in the canon repo: `node packs/claudinite-growth/capture-log.mjs --issue <n>`). Skip only if
   the repo doesn't declare `claudinite-growth`. A later merge in the same session runs it again.
7. Run the basics pack's
   [verify-in-production](../../../basics/skills/verify-in-production/SKILL.md) skill, unasked.
   This step is that skill's **only** trigger — it files against what the squash actually landed,
   which is why it runs here and not when the code was written or the PR opened. It decides
   whether this change needs a production check at all — most don't — and files the issue that
   comes back once the change is live. Never offer the owner to check later instead.

Don't re-read the issue to confirm it closed — `Closes #<issue>` does that on merge.
