1	# Working discipline
2	
3	The working discipline that isn't itself a GitHub operation — general habits for how to approach a
4	change, independent of any one project.
5	
6	- **Starting any requested change** — begin from the *problem*, not the solution, in any
7	  repository and not just this one. Reach an explicit shared understanding with the owner of the
8	  problem the change is meant to solve **and** agreement that the requested change is the best way
9	  to solve it; a different fix, or none, may serve better.
10	
11	- **Replying to an owner comment** — open with an explicit classification line,
12	  `Comment class: correction | feature | process-change | other`, where `other` covers questions,
13	  approvals and command phrases and a mixed comment names each part. An automation dispatch prompt
14	  is a comment too: class `other`, in your *first* substantive reply rather than at the end of the
15	  run. Put the class **alone on the line** and any explanation on the next one: the line is scanned
16	  for *every* class token on it, so restating the menu declares all of them. A class cannot be taken
17	  back, and a clean re-declaration further down does not override the first.
18	
19	- **Acting on a correction** — you misunderstood something. Repair the shared understanding, then
20	  rework what the misread already touched; the artifact changes as much as the correction demands,
21	  but a correction never adds a new requirement or rule.
22	
23	- **Acting on a feature** — agree on the requirement, record it in the project's requirements
24	  document (its executable spec, where it keeps one), write the test that proves it and watch it
25	  fail, then implement until it passes.
26	
27	- **Acting on a process change** — the owner is changing *how* work is done. Land it as durable
28	  rules in the project's local scope, its own local packs (in Claudinite itself, its packs), routed
29	  through the mechanism promotion ladder (platform setting → hook → check → skill → prose).
30	  Promoting a rule into the shared canon is the growth lifecycle's separate call, not the
31	  interactive session's.
32	
33	- **Choosing what goes on that ladder** — only a rule that constrains *how work is done* and
34	  outlives any one feature; a checkable signature doesn't earn a rule its place. Reject two shapes
35	  outright: a check that asserts particular code exists or still reads a particular way (it pins a
36	  point in time), and a rule derivable from the product's requirements (that is a requirement —
37	  take it to the feature path, the requirements document and the test that proves it).
38	
39	- **Landing a rule anywhere on the ladder** — author the assurance first, the check the future
40	  world must satisfy, execute it and watch it fail, and only then make the fixes that turn it green.
41	  At the prose rung, where no check can carry an in-flight judgment rule, the equivalent step is
42	  showing the corpus doesn't already cover the rule before writing it.
43	
44	- **Building a mechanism for a behavior** — verify against a real run that it isn't already
45	  provided.
46	
47	- **Building release, deploy, versioning or CI plumbing** — look for the shared pack that owns it
48	  first; copying a mechanic from a sibling repo is the tell that it belongs centrally. If no pack
49	  owns it, report the gap rather than author a third copy.
50	
51	- **Finishing a change** — watch it work **now**; never park it on "check tomorrow". What a task
52	  costs is its shelf-life, the time from starting it until everyone can forget about it.
53	
54	- **Changing scheduled or unattended machinery** — force a run now (the scheduler's wake lever, a
55	  `workflow_dispatch`, the fleet-wide force sweep) and watch it to a terminal state rather than wait
56	  for its next natural run.
57	
58	- **Planning a migration** — prefer the design that converges in one forced pass to the one that
59	  trickles across nightly cycles, accept legacy input at the door so nothing has to wait for
60	  stragglers, and drive the stragglers with a standing mechanism rather than a phase someone must
61	  remember to close. Write every phase's code — the cleanup and the destructive tail included —
62	  before asking for approval, and chain each execution step to the verification of the one before
63	  it rather than to anyone's memory;
64	  [writing-migration-plans](skills/writing-migration-plans/SKILL.md) owns that ordering and the
65	  chain's mechanics.
66	
67	- **When verifying now is genuinely impossible** (an external release window, an upstream fix in
68	  flight, an effect that only appears once the change is deployed, converged or loaded by a later
69	  session) — the follow-up is a mechanism that comes to you, never a human's memory and never an
70	  offer to the owner to go and check later. File it with
71	  [verify-in-production](skills/verify-in-production/SKILL.md), unasked, **once the PR has
72	  merged** and never before — a PR can be rejected, and a still-open branch can be rewritten
73	  under you, either of which strands a verification whose premise never reached `main`. The
74	  skill owns both halves — whether this change needs one at all (most don't; a test that ran is
75	  already the mechanism), and the issue that states what puts the change in production and what
76	  proves it works there.
77	
78	- **Finishing a larger element** — one that earned a design doc or a phased tracking issue — a
79	  point verification is not enough: schedule the review that comes back once the element has
80	  lived in production about a week, asking whether it is working, misused, overused or underused
81	  against its real record — with the brief written at design time, expected amounts, signals and
82	  the metrics that measure them included, never improvised when the review runs.
83	  [production-retrospective](skills/production-retrospective/SKILL.md) owns the trigger, the
84	  brief, and the lane's other classes — canon, local-pack and fleet alike.
85	
86	- **Receiving feedback that flags a misunderstanding** — check whether the artifact is already
87	  correct before expanding it; if it is, say so and push back rather than edit.
88	
89	- **Writing anything** — size it to its idea: "open one issue" takes a sentence, not three
90	  paragraphs.
91	
92	- **Correcting or auditing an artifact against an authoritative source** — derive the corrected
93	  version from the *source* before reading the existing draft, then diff against the old draft to
94	  surface what was actually wrong.
95	
96	- **Acting on an approval to merge, ship or proceed** — it applies only *backward*, to the work
97	  already in front of the owner when it's given, never to anything requested or done *after* it. A
98	  later follow-up, even a fix to the just-approved change, needs its own explicit approval — and a
99	  multiple-choice answer is not an approval at all, even when an option's wording mentioned the
100	  action.
101	
102	## Harness-tool contracts
103	
104	Contracts worth knowing before you spend a call rediscovering them.
105	
106	- **Searching for a tool with `ToolSearch`** — a search that finds nothing is evidence about your
107	  query, not about the environment. Search the fully-qualified name (`select:mcp__<server>__<tool>`,
108	  copied off the deferred-tools listing) and try the tool before telling the owner a step is theirs;
109	  the bare short name returns "no matching tools", which reads exactly like absence.
110	
111	- **Calling `Edit`** — the file must have been read *with the read tool*; `cat`/`grep`/`sed` don't
112	  count. The moment shell output tells you which file you're about to change, read that exact path;
113	  a narrow offset window satisfies it.
114	
115	- **Calling `Grep` with a context flag** (`-n`/`-A`/`-B`/`-C`) — it's silently ignored under the
116	  default `output_mode: "files_with_matches"`, so the call answers only a match count or file
117	  list, never the lines you asked for, with no error to catch it. Pass `output_mode: "content"`
118	  in the same call as any context flag.

# Version history

Records for `packs/claudinite-tasks/pack.mjs`'s `version` field, one row per bump.

| Version | Date | What changed |
|---|---|---|
<<<<<<< HEAD
| 60831.7 | 2026-08-31 | The janitor gains rule H, the unclosed terminal: an open item wearing `task:status:done` or `task:status:rejected` is a transition that tore — every writer closes in the same breath — so it reads as finished to every other rule and to the leash while sitting open in the queue forever. The close is the whole repair, at the status's own outcome, with no relabelling. Two guards against a converge in flight, an hour's clock and a fresh read before acting (#1526). |
=======
| 60831.7 | 2026-08-31 | Coded production validations (#1530): a verification whose artifact is a URL routes to the new agentless `verify-production` task, whose worker fetches declarative `Live-probe:`/`Verify-probe:` lines Action-side — where egress exists — and judges them in code: liveness failing re-arms the item, a verify probe failing against a live release reopens `Original-issue:`, all passing closes with the evidence read. The re-arm rides a new code-work protocol: a worker printing `claudinite-requeue: <instant> — <reason>` before a clean exit has the executor stamp the item's `Not-before` (machine half) and return it to blocked instead of closing done — the third answer an exit code could not give. |
>>>>>>> 0787cdd (claudinite-tasks: verify-production, the coded production-validation task)
| 60831.6 | 2026-08-31 | A migration record carries `CLAUDINITE_VARS: ${{ toJSON(vars) }}` into each member's LIVE executor workflow, so a member that adopted before #1494 stops holding the bag reader with no bag to read. A rewrite rather than a materialize, anchored above the `# claudinite:secrets` marker: the executor is not identical across members and a wholesale copy would take each one's stamped `required_secrets` with it. Needs `claudinite-lifecycle` 60831.1's withhold lane to deliver (#1518). |
| 60831.5 | 2026-08-31 | Janitor rule E never supersedes an AD-HOC park: every ad-hoc item runs the same task, so a later run of it is evidence about that run and not about this issue's own work. Two verification issues were closed on a third issue's evidence, their own `Verify:` assertion never executed (#1498). |
| 60831.4 | 2026-08-31 | The scheduler run's work-item list reads membership through `isQueueItem`, the shared predicate, rather than the `[claudinite-work]` title prefix — an adopted marked issue keeps the person's own title forever, so the prefix test dropped exactly that class from the one job that releases a blocked item, and ad-hoc items slept days past their `Not-before:` (#1497). The executing-leash reclaim reads such an item's task off its worker path too, so `implement-request`'s `on_interrupt: 'needs-human'` is honoured rather than silently re-queued. |
| 60831.3 | 2026-08-31 | The executor carries every repository VARIABLE as one static `CLAUDINITE_VARS: ${{ toJSON(vars) }}` line, so a task needing a repo variable no longer needs the workflow to name it — the human-merged-PR-per-value coupling that still binds secrets. `vars-bag.mjs` reads it and `taskEnv` unpacks it additively, never overwriting a name the runner's environment already carries; unlike the secrets bag there is no per-task selection, `vars` being non-sensitive by construction. `toJSON(secrets)` stays guarded out of both stubs (#1492). |
| 60831.2 | 2026-08-31 | `converge-item.mjs` is stated and built as what it is: the transition a work-item SESSION performs, planned in code. `instructions.md` step 6 is its only caller, so the REST executor beside it was unreachable — and reached first, making a session meet an error before the path written for it and report that it could not converge. That is what left finished runs to the janitor's 3h leash, which parks them `needs-human-decision`. The file now plans and prints, always on stdout and exit 0; the item is handed in with `--item-file` instead of a second run behind an environment variable. The Actions-side transition is untouched in `executor.mjs` (#1491). |

attachment.content:
- adopt-pack: Add one or more packs to an already-adopted Claudinite member — declare, run each pack's adoption interview, re-vendor, scaffold, land. Use when asked to adopt, add, enable, or declare a pack (e.g. product-wiki, executable-requirements) on a repo that already runs Claudinite.
- verify-in-production: Decide whether a change that has merged can only be proven in production, and if so file the verification that comes back on its own once it is live. Use immediately after the merge, beside the conversation capture — never before, and not on request.
- writing-migration-plans: Where a plan and a design live, and how to order a plan's phases so nothing stalls mid-run — the plan is a tracking issue (never a plan document in the repo), the design doc carries only the end state with rationale and alternatives; front-load the out-of-band setup, write ALL the code including the cleanup and take one approval for the stack, then chain every execution step to the verification of the one before it as a queued continuation, and keep the tracking issue append-only while implementing. Use BEFORE writing any DESIGN.md, migration plan, phased implementation plan, rollout or cutover plan — including the moment you are about to create a docs/<initiative>/ file — and when working through a plan's tracking issue.

content.subject: File the GitHub issue for coded production validations
content.description: Lifecycle step 1: an issue describing the requirement — a coded (non-agentic) production-validation lane: URL fetch + declarative query, runs Action-side where egress exists, re-arms while not-yet-live, reopens the original issue on failure.

content.subject: Add the requeue protocol to the queue engine
content.description: A code worker printing `claudinite-requeue: <ISO> — <reason>` on an ok exit makes the executor stamp Not-before (machine block) and swap running-executor → blocked instead of closing done. Reader in code-work.mjs, handling in executor.mjs; tests first, watch them fail.

content.subject: Build the verify-production task (probe grammar + worker)
content.description: packs/claudinite-tasks/tasks/verify-production/: agentless manual task; probes.mjs parses `Live-probe:`/`Verify-probe:` lines (url :: assertion — status/contains/matches/json ops) and evaluates them over injected fetch; worker.mjs reads the item's human text, runs probes, requeues when not live, comments evidence and closes on pass, reopens Original-issue on fail.

content.subject: Update the verify-in-production skill and its prose tests
content.description: The coded form becomes the preferred lane for URL-readable artifacts; the "can the RUN read it" gate gains it; the filer forces a run now and watches it report not-yet-live (see-it-fail). Keep the agentic form for GitHub-tool reads.
